title: What if you could hear through your feet, like an elephant?

narration.heading: The ground hums
narration.text: You're standing barefoot, and the ground starts to hum. Someone far away is calling you.

narration.heading: Deep rumbles
narration.text: Elephants talk in deep rumbles, as low as fourteen hertz. That's below what your ears can hear.

narration.heading: Loud
narration.text: Some African elephant rumbles hit a hundred and seventeen decibels.

narration.heading: How it works
narration.text: Here's the trick. The rumble shakes the ground, and the vibration travels through the earth.

narration.heading: Feet that hear
narration.text: Elephants feel it through the skin of their feet and trunk.

narration.heading: Listening pose
narration.text: To listen, they lean forward onto their front feet, or lift one foreleg off the ground.

narration.heading: Built-in sensors
narration.text: The cushion pads of their feet even contain little nodes of cartilage.

narration.heading: The twist
narration.text: The twist? Rumble vibrations may carry about sixteen kilometres through the ground. Stomping may reach even farther.

narration.heading: Your call
narration.text: With elephant feet, you could feel a friend calling from far away. Would you take your shoes off?

hook.banner: What if you could hear through your feet?

skit.text: Hearing through my feet? I don't have feet. Just very sensitive wheels.

titles: What if you could hear through your feet, like an elephant?
Elephants can hear with their feet
youtube.description: How elephants send deep rumbles through the ground and feel them through their feet and trunks, and how far those vibrations can travel.

sources.claim: Asian elephant rumbles are 14–24 Hz; African elephant calls range 15–35 Hz and can be as loud as 117 dB; the vibrations are detected by the skin of the feet and trunk; listening elephants lean forward or lift a foreleg; foot pads contain cartilaginous nodes; rumble waveforms travel about 16 km and locomotion signals up to 32 km
Human hearing is commonly given as 20 to 20,000 Hz; elephants can hear sounds at 16 Hz–12 kHz
Elephant seismic signals from rumbles travel about 16 km and from stomping or mock charging up to 32 km
